Try to fix the phonetic pronunciation by getting rid of a few letters and letter combinations...

Ph becomes F... i.e. Philosophy becomes Filosofy.... The only reason we use it is because Ph makes a "Fff" sound in latin. And academics in the 17th century wanted to show how smart and educated they were by using latin pronunciation. (snobbery).

Qu becomes Q.. The only reason we have to place a U after every Q is because early printing technology often made it hard to distinguish Q's from O's. Putting the U after a Q made it clear. That's no longer a problem and we have no need to maintain this outdated 'hack'.

ck becomes k......
As above, the c was added to words like hack, back, stack etc because early printing presses often produced K's that were hard to read. The c added an additional 'Kaa' sound to ensure the reader was sure of the intended pronunciation.

Get rid of the letters C, X and change the pronunciation of G.

C alternately produces the sound 'Ka' as in Cat, or "Sss" as in Cease. There's no instance where the letter C can't be replaced by either an S or a K. It's a completely unnecessary letter, and it's changing pronunciation causes pointless confusion.

X either produces the sound 'Zzz' as in Xylophone, or 'Kssss' as in "sex". Again an unnecessary letter that can be removed from the language without any noticeable effect.

G either produces a hard sound as in "Gap", or a soft sound as in "Marge". The soft sound is identical to the sound a J makes. G should always make the hard sound, and any instances of the soft sound should be replaced with J. i.e. George, would be spelled Jorje, Gorge becomes Gorje, Garage would be spelled Garaje.

And no more silent letters, they're the very definition of unnecessary.

Dear Mint Users,

If you run into the following message during bootup after installing Mint 17.3 and NVidia DIsplay drivers: **Boot Error - ACPI PCC Probe Failed **there is a temporary solution I'm using to avoid having to look at this message constantly on bootup.

This solution works for me however may not work for you depending on your hardware configuration. Double click on the Update Manager Shield at the bottom right of the screen and select View > Kernels. I'm currently using 4.0.2-27 without any issues.

The error message if you get on bootup Boot Error - ACPI PCC Probe Failed when using Mint 17.3 is believed to be harmless. For the most part you will be able to bootup just fine. But if you are like me don't like these annoying messages selecting a different kernel will resolve the issue however keep in mind some kernels are not stable and it's best to use your recommended kernel Mint has provided.

[Do NOT do this unless you know what you're doing or have your data backed up.]
